text:
Alex K: Quick heads-up — during the mini-inspect canary I noticed we sometimes surface full responses in the debug stream even when the route is set to 'minimal'.
Maya R: Ugh. Is that from the fallback routing path or a scrub failure? :eyes:
Alex K: Seems like fallback + KV-cache replay. Repro steps short: hit /v1/chat with debug_token=allowlist-xyz, then inc a model fallback -> response contains unredacted snippet.
Jordan L: Can you paste the request/resp sample (redacted) and the routing header?
Alex K: pasted snippet: ```
{
  "path": "/v1/chat",
  "headers": {"x-rw-debug-token": "allowlist-xyz", "x-rw-route": "canary-east"},
  "response": "<REDACTED>... name: John Doe ... <REDACTED>"
}```
Samir P: Thanks. Two quick ideas: (1) tighten the debug_token TTL & scope (shorter lifetime, per-tenant secret), (2) change inspect path to only send hashed payloads unless inspect-mode=full allowed.
Maya R: I like (2). We should document where we allow full payloads: only on dedicated/internally-approved tenants.
Jordan L: Operational risk: if we hash everything then qa can't reproduce subtle prompts. Maybe support an ephemeral unmask flow: temp-unmask token exchanged for a one-time signed assertion. TTL=5m, one-time-use.
Alex K: That aligns w/privilege separation. Also need a sampling cap so we don't saturate audit pipelines. Proposal: per-tenant debug quota + global guardrail. Example config: 
```json
{"debug_quota": {"per_tenant_per_hour": 10, "global_burst": 50}, "unmask_ttl_secs": 300, "allowlist_mode": "strict"}
```
Samir P: For PII redaction rules, prefer a layered approach: heuristics -> deterministic HMAC pseudonymization -> redaction. Heuristics flag candidates, HMAC with tenant key for traceability, redact only on downstream exports.
Maya R: We must be explicit in Console UX: show when a sample is HMAC'd vs redacted vs full. Ops wants to be able to filter by 'pseudonymized' vs 'redacted'.
Jordan L: Implementation detail: use keyed HMAC with per-tenant rotation. Keep a 'rotation-v' in audit. People can map pseudonyms via legal/gated flows.
Alex K: About routing: mini-inspect should honor primary routing policy first. If fallback to cheaper model happens, mini-inspect must drop full-response unless allowlist+unmask.
Samir P: Agree. Also add a sampling 'inspect-weight' signal to router so we don't route debug traffic to sensitive capacity zones.
Maya R: UX question — how will SRE request temporary unmask for a support ticket? We need an in-console button that records the approval. No CLI-only flows.
Jordan L: +1. Button should create an audit event with requester's identity and TTL start. Then the token is issued and logged.
Alex K: Action items: 1) eng-platform: codify debug_token TTL and one-time-unmask flow (Samir), 2) eng-sre: add console button + audit event (Maya), 3) eng-runtime: enforce drop-on-fallback unless unmask present (Jordan).
Samir P: I'll draft RFC for unmask flow with HMAC pseudonymization and sampling quotas. Will include rate-limits: 1 unmask token per 5 minutes per tenant, global 20/min.
Maya R: I'll mock the console approval UI and add label states: "pseudonymized", "redacted", "full (audit-only)".
telemetry-bot: ingest.alert: mini-inspect: debug-token use increased 3x in last 10m for canary-east (rate 34/min)
Alex K: Oof. Can we throttle canary-east debug flows until quotas land?
Samir P: I'll flip a transient guard to block debug-token from canary-east for 30m and notify support.
Maya R: please add a slack alert to #incidents and tag SRE on the guard.
Jordan L: Noted. I'll add testcases for fallback drop and unmask exchange to the runtime test-suite.
Alex K: Thanks team. Let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to sign off on RFC + console mock. :thumbsup:
